quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #2
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What color are temporary signs in construction and maintenance work areas?

options.text: Red background with green writing.
Orange background with black writing.
Yellow background with blue writing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Orange background with black writing.
questions.explanation: Temporary signs in work zones have orange backgrounds with black writing and symbols.

questions.question: When driving in fog, which headlights should you use?

options.text: High beam headlights.
Low beam headlights.
Four-way flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, or snow. High beams reflect off moisture and reduce visibility.

questions.question: When crossing a sidewalk to enter or exit a driveway, drivers must:

options.text: Have the right-of-way.
Yield to pedestrians.
Honk to clear a path.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Drivers must yield to pedestrians when crossing a sidewalk to enter or exit a driveway, alley, or parking lot.

questions.question: Who can use handicap parking spaces?

options.text: Anyone if all other spaces are full.
Only drivers with a handicap license plate or tag.
People who are not feeling well.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only drivers with a handicap license plate or tag.
questions.explanation: Only people with disabilities can park in handicap spaces. You must display a valid handicap license plate or hanging tag.

questions.question: In rain or fog, drivers should use their:

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in rain, snow, sleet, or fog. High beams reflect off water and reduce visibility.

questions.question: A driver should watch:

options.text: Directly in front of the car.
Only the middle of the road.
The sides, front, and back of the car.

questions.correctAnswerText: The sides, front, and back of the car.
questions.explanation: Good drivers watch all around their vehicle—to the sides, ahead, and behind. This helps you know what is happening in every direction.

questions.question: After drinking several beers, alcohol effects will only go away by:

options.text: Taking a cold shower.
Waiting several hours.
Drinking coffee.

questions.correctAnswerText: Waiting several hours.
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body. Coffee, exercise, or cold showers do not speed this up. One drink takes about one hour to wear off.

questions.question: A school bus ahead has flashing red lights. What should you do?

options.text: Stop and go when you think children have exited.
Slow to 25 mph and pass carefully.
Stop until the red lights stop flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the red lights stop flashing.
questions.explanation: You must stop and stay stopped when a school bus has flashing red lights. Do not move until the lights stop flashing.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Do it quickly and often.
Change lanes when a car is in your blind spot.
Do it gradually and carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do it gradually and carefully.
questions.explanation: Always change lanes gradually and carefully. Only change when needed. Each lane change raises the risk of an accident.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle is approaching with flashing red or blue lights. What should you do?

options.text: Pull to the right and stop.
Keep driving but stay out of its way.
Drive faster to reach your destination first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: Move to the right edge of the road and stop for police cars, fire trucks, and ambulances using sirens and flashing lights. If in an intersection, drive through first, then pull over.

questions.question: As blood alcohol concentration (BAC) increases, you become:

options.text: More intoxicated.
More sober.
More coordinated.

questions.correctAnswerText: More intoxicated.
questions.explanation: BAC measures the percentage of alcohol in your blood. The higher your BAC, the more impaired you are.

questions.question: If a car has airbags, should you wear a seat belt?

options.text: Yes, seat belts should still be worn.
No, seat belts are not needed.
Wear seat belts behind your back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, seat belts should still be worn.
questions.explanation: Airbags are important safety devices. For the best protection, use seat belts together with airbags.

questions.question: If you feel drowsy while driving, you should:

options.text: Try to stay awake.
Take a break.
Take caffeine pills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a break.
questions.explanation: Stop at the nearest rest area to nap, stretch, or change drivers. Caffeine pills are not a safe replacement for rest.

questions.question: What does this yellow sign mean?

options.text: The road ahead has many curves.
There is a sharp curve in the road ahead.
The road ahead may be slippery.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead may be slippery.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road may be slippery when wet.

questions.question: A traffic light is green, but a police officer signals you to stop. What should you do?

options.text: Obey the officer.
Obey the traffic signal.
Do what the vehicle in front of you does.

questions.correctAnswerText: Obey the officer.
questions.explanation: Always obey a police officer's directions, even if they conflict with traffic signals, signs, or road markings.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: There is a 35 mph speed zone after the curve ahead.
Drive no slower than 35 mph around the upcoming curve.
Slow down to 35 mph or less before entering the upcoming curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to 35 mph or less before entering the upcoming curve.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs show conditions ahead. Speed advisory signs tell you the safe speed for the upcoming curve or hazard.

questions.question: You are driving behind a large truck on the freeway. How should you drive?

options.text: Closer behind the truck than you would behind a passenger vehicle.
Farther behind the truck than you would behind a passenger vehicle.
To the right side of the truck and wait to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther behind the truck than you would behind a passenger vehicle.
questions.explanation: Keep extra distance behind large trucks because they have large blind spots and need more space to stop.

questions.question: What does a steady green traffic light mean?

options.text: Increase your speed.
Adjust your mirrors.
You may go through the intersection at a safe speed if it is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may go through the intersection at a safe speed if it is clear.
questions.explanation: A green light means you can proceed. Always check that the intersection is clear and yield to any traffic or pedestrians still crossing.

questions.question: Your car breaks down on an interstate. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn at passing cars to get their attention.
Get out and flag down the first vehicle that passes.
Pull off the road, turn on your emergency flashers, and stay in your vehicle if you can.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull off the road, turn on your emergency flashers, and stay in your vehicle if you can.
questions.explanation: Turn on your emergency flashers to warn other drivers. Stay inside your vehicle because standing on an interstate is dangerous due to fast traffic.

questions.question: What is a crosswalk?

options.text: Another name for a four-way intersection.
An area for road construction workers.
The area where pedestrians cross the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: The area where pedestrians cross the roadway.
questions.explanation: Crosswalks are marked by white lines to show where pedestrians should cross. Some crosswalks are unmarked.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow arrow on a traffic signal mean?

options.text: Speed up so you can turn before the light changes.
You do not need to signal your turn.
Get ready to stop and let oncoming traffic go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get ready to stop and let oncoming traffic go first.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow arrow means the protected turn is ending. Prepare to stop and yield to oncoming traffic before turning.

questions.question: Why should you not stop suddenly in front of a large truck or bus?

options.text: Small vehicle drivers cannot see large trucks in their rearview mirrors.
Large trucks and buses need longer distances to stop because of their size and weight.
Large trucks and buses drive faster than small vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks and buses need longer distances to stop because of their size and weight.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles need more distance to stop. A sudden stop in front of them may cause a collision because the driver cannot brake in time.

questions.question: Which of these causes traffic crashes?

options.text: Speeding and driving too fast for conditions.
Getting enough rest and staying alert.
Watching the road and focusing on driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speeding and driving too fast for conditions.
questions.explanation: Speeding and driving too fast for road conditions cause many crashes. Always drive within the speed limit and adjust your speed to conditions.

questions.question: What can you do to reduce road rage?

options.text: Always signal when changing lanes.
Talk on your cell phone while driving.
Use your horn frequently.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always signal when changing lanes.
questions.explanation: To prevent road rage, follow all traffic laws and signals. Always signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: Reaction time is slower after:

options.text: Drinking alcohol.
Sleeping.
Working hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drinking alcohol.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reflexes, reduces your vision, and hurts your judgment. It makes you a dangerous driver.
